subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — Orchid Labs POC next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah@orchidlabs.ai>, Dan Lee <dan.lee@orchidlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T18:02:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood vs competitors (bake-off)

Hi Sarah / Dan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand where Orchid Labs is on the model infra side. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have everything in one place.

Pain points you described
- 99th pct latency spikes during peak traffic (alerts on production routes at ~700–900ms for short prompts)
- Rising token bill for embeddings and chat features — looking to cut per-inference cost by ~30%
- Multi-region failover: need predictable behavior in us-east-1 + eu-west-1 with no data leakage
- Security: SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration required for PII-sensitive routing

Goals for the bake-off / POC
1) Reduce tail latency for short prompts (<250ms 99th pct) while maintaining throughput
2) Demonstrate a 25–35% improvement in tokens/$ for your typical request mix
3) Show seamless local residency (us-east-1) and KMS keying for sensitive routes

Decision criteria you mentioned
- Latency (99th pct) and jitter under load
- Unit economics (tokens/$) across chat + embeddings mix
- Ops overhead (how much engineering lift to maintain)
- Security/compliance evidence (SOC 2 / KMS / audit logs)

Competitive notes from the call
- BigCloud AI: strong managed latency but cost is high and limited privacy guarantees
- ModelHub OSS: low inference cost with quantized runtimes but requires ops investment for reliability
- Redwood: unified runtime with automatic batching/caching, can run in VPC or Dedicated for isolation — POC will validate the profile for your workload

Open questions / items we need from you
- Canonical sample workload (anonymized request logs + example prompts) — to run replayed benchmarks
- Security questionnaire / any additional compliance constraints beyond SOC 2
- Target POC window: you suggested week of May 9 — confirm availability

Proposed POC tests (we suggested):
A) Baseline latency test (10k requests, representative prompt distribution) — compare 50/95/99 pcts
B) Throughput scaling test (sustained 500 rps for 30 min) to evaluate autoscaling behavior
C) Cost run: run a 24-hour steady-state trace to estimate tokens/$ for your mix
D) Security & ops: verify KMS integration and audit log delivery to your SIEM in us-east-1

Attachments: competitive_matrix.xlsx (vendor feature matrix), poc_instructions.pdf (proposed test scripts & samples).

Next steps (proposed)
1) You share anonymized sample traffic + security questionnaire by EOD Tue (May 4)
2) We provision a POC environment scoped for the tests and share baseline runtimes by May 7
3) Bake-off execution week: May 9–13 (we'll run tests, present results, then sync)

I'll also loop in Marissa on pricing/contracting so we can prep a one-month Dedicated trial if the POC looks good. Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
Attachment: competitive_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)
Attachment: poc_instructions.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Sarah Thompson <sarah@orchidlabs.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Dan Lee <dan.lee@orchidlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood vs competitors (bake-off)

Thanks Aditya — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from Orchid: 

- Security: our security team will need SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of KMS integration. We can share the completed questionnaire by EOD Monday.
- Data residency: POC must run in us-east-1; production preference is us-east-1 with failover to eu-west-1 for latency-sensitive routes.
- Timing: May 9–13 works for the engineering team for the bake-off.

Open items we can provide this week
- Anonymized request logs (redacted PII) — we'll send a 48-hour sample tomorrow.
- Primary decision owners: me (Head of ML Infra) and Dan (Platform Eng) — they'll run the acceptance tests during the POC.

One question: do you have a simple script we can run on our side to validate vendor latency (client-side vs server-side measurements)? Would prefer consistent measurement harness across vendors.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Thompson
Head of ML Infrastructure, Orchid Labs
sarah@orchidlabs.ai

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood vs competitors (bake-off)

Thanks Sarah — good call. We'll provide: 

1) A small open-source measurement harness (script + README) that runs client-side latency checks and server-side timing (attached to the POC repo). The script will generate the same prompt distribution we use in Redwood's baseline.
2) Baseline report: I'll run our internal baseline against your sample traffic as soon as we get it and share redwood-performance-report.pdf by May 7.
3) SOC2: Attached is our SOC 2 summary + pointer to the full report (we can set up an NDA'd exchange if needed).

Proposed POC schedule (tight):
- May 4: Receive anonymized logs + completed security questionnaire
- May 5–7: Provision POC infra in us-east-1 and run baseline tests
- May 9–13: Bake-off run and joint validation sessions (we'll share live dashboards)
- May 14: Findings review and go/no-go

If that timeline looks good I'll ask Marissa to prepare a one-month Dedicated pricing SKU and a short MSA for the POC. Also, Dan — if you have any specific production traffic patterns (spikes by hour) call them out so we can model them in the throughput test.

Thanks again,
Aditya

Attachment: redwood-performance-report.pdf (interim placeholder, will update after baselines)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:20:00Z
Subject: Internal: Orchid Labs bake-off — pricing + discount guidance

Marissa — quick internal note following up on the Orchid thread (they confirmed May 9–13).

Summary of ask: they want a one-month Dedicated trial scoped to peak capacity of ~500 rps sustained for throughput tests and baseline latency runs. If POC results meet targets, they'll evaluate 12-month reserved capacity.

Key negotiation points to consider:
- Trial pricing: recommend a trial SKU with a 30% introductory discount to Dedicated list for one month (we can recoup in committed contract)
- SLA ask: they want 99.9% availability for the trial window (we can offer operational support but keep enterprise SLA contingent on longer commit)
- Security: they will need SOC2 evidence and KMS integration — factor in any additional onboarding hours for Private/VPC setup if required

Attachments included in the external thread (for reference): competitive_matrix.xlsx, poc_instructions.pdf, redwood-performance-report.pdf

Can you draft a short trial SKU + estimated MRR delta? Also, flag any capacity constraints for May 9–13 (GPU pool reservations).

Thanks — Aditya
